message: No detected input validation: The code reads CSV files directly via pandas without any schema checks, dtype assertions, shape validations, or value-range guards on the loaded data.

No detected untrusted source handling: Data is loaded from local file paths only (e.g., 'data/rand_select_400_avg.csv'); there are no remote fetches and therefore no checksum verification, authentication, or integrity checks.
No detected label flipping detection: No label distribution comparison, expected-set validation, or label-noise detection tool (e.g., Cleanlab) is used anywhere in the data preparation flow.
No detected data poisoning defenses: The code performs no outlier detection, statistical anomaly checks, or filtering of suspicious samples on the training data before use.

No detected model integrity verification: The code loads serialized models via joblib's `load()` (e.g., `load(log_dir + '/best_model')`) without any hash check, signature verification, or pinned revision to ensure integrity.
No detected label distribution validation: No code checks class balance, verifies expected label sets, or detects anomalous label distributions before training begins.
No detected backdoor or trigger detection: There is no activation analysis, trigger detection, or gradient anomaly detection anywhere in the training pipeline.
No detected differential privacy: No differential privacy library (Opacus, TensorFlow Privacy, DP-SGD, etc.) is imported or used in the training code.
No detected adversarial robustness testing: No adversarial robustness libraries (Foolbox, ART, FGSM, PGD) or stress tests are used anywhere in the evaluation code.
No detected input sanitization: The code loads CSV files directly via pandas and passes data to models without any shape, range, type, or schema validation checks.
No detected output bounds checks: Model predictions are used directly for metrics and confusion matrices with no NaN guards, probability sanity checks, or threshold validation on outputs.
No detected prompt injection defenses: The pipeline uses classical ML models (decision tree, SVM, XGBoost, etc.), not LLMs, so prompt injection defenses are not applicable.
